correction_reason: The existing summary describes the paper’s compression results, while the selected unresolved passage concerns transfer of exact exponential-time algorithm improvements.
sentences: Boolean Max-CSP assigns values to variables to maximize the total weight of satisfied constraints from a fixed finite language.
The degree of that language is the largest degree of the multilinear real polynomials representing its Boolean constraints.
The paper transfers exponential-time speedups between degree-d Max-CSP and Max d-CNF-SAT when negative weights are allowed, and removes that allowance for some constraint languages.
The question asks whether a speedup for a degree-d Max-CSP with nonnegative integer weights also yields a speedup for Max d-CNF-SAT.
Resolving the remaining cases would show whether polynomial degree also organizes exact exponential-time complexity in the usual nonnegative-weight setting.

correction_reason: The existing summary incorrectly interprets counting as counting possible repairs; the source concerns how edits are counted against the modification budget.
sentences: A relation-modification problem asks whether a logical structure can be made to satisfy a fixed property using edits within a budget.
The paper compares conventions such as counting modified tuples across all relations, within one relation, or separately for each relation.
Its classifications coincide for arbitrary relational structures and directed graphs under the studied conventions, including charging for ordered versus unordered tuples.
The question asks whether another natural way of measuring the modification budget, potentially motivated by database repair, makes the complexity of these two settings differ.
This would reveal whether their apparent computational equivalence depends on how the cost of changing data is measured.
